channel.title: SecurityWizardry Vulnerability Radar (RMFconsultoria)
channel.description: Alertas de vulnerabilidade (CVSS) - fonte NVD (fallback quando o SecurityWizardry está bloqueado) - RMFconsultoria

item.title: CVE-2026-131281 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with asset edit permission could change the approval requirements and effective automation user for an asset without Splunk SOAR recording field-level audit details for those changes. This could weaken investigation and accountability for changes to security-sensitive asset settings. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not include the asset approval voting fields and effective automation user field in its field-level audit coverage.

item.title: CVE-2026-131282 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who holds the "Observer" Splunk SOAR role could access a password-reset credential in a diagnostic log bundle and reset the password for an active local account. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not redact password-reset email bodies before it logs communications between product processes.

item.title: CVE-2026-131283 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with playbook edit permission could cause later playbook conversions to include spurious branch conditions. This can prevent downstream blocks from running in affected converted playbooks. The vulnerability is possible because the playbook converter retains branch conditions from previous conversions.

item.title: CVE-2026-131284 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view and edit containers could import a container archive that makes artifacts appear to be part of a case or have notes when no corresponding case associations or notes exist. This could cause Representational State Transfer (REST) API clients and filters to use incorrect artifact state. The vulnerability is possible because container archive import accepts artifact workflow state from the archive instead of deriving that state from associated cases and notes. For more information see Splunk SOAR REST API reference (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-131285 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who can edit and run playbooks could cause automation batches for other events to stop running. The vulnerability occurs because Splunk SOAR does not bind playbook API requests to the server-provided execution context.

item.title: CVE-2026-131286 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.1 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to author and run playbooks could view action data outside the authorized scope for that user and change the status and message of another playbook run. The vulnerability is possible because the playbook API does not verify that the requested playbook run is within the authorized scope of the authenticated user.

item.title: CVE-2026-131287 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 9.6
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 9.6 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Playbooks view, edit, execute, and delete permissions could cause existing cross-repository playbook references to run attacker-controlled playbook code. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR can bind existing cross-repository playbook references to a different source control repository when a deleted repository name is reused.

item.title: CVE-2026-131288 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.3 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with access to the configured load balancer account could replace a load balancer helper that Splunk SOAR later runs with root privileges during cluster lifecycle operations. If a Splunk SOAR administrator performs a cluster lifecycle operation, Splunk SOAR could execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the load balancer. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify the integrity or ownership of the load balancer helper before running it with root privileges.

item.title: CVE-2026-131289 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 3.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 3.1 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who holds a role that can edit and run playbooks in Splunk SOAR could cause Splunk SOAR to run non-read-only actions from a Safe Mode playbook, resulting in unauthorized state changes. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify that the playbook run context in an action request matches the context that the server provided.

item.title: CVE-2026-131290 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to edit and run playbooks could view child playbook status and loop-state metadata for playbook runs outside the authorized scope for that user. The vulnerability is possible because the playbook status API does not bind the requested run to the current execution context before it returns metadata.

item.title: CVE-2026-131291 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a Splunk SOAR user who can edit and run playbooks for a permitted container label could associate action and callback state with a running playbook outside that container label. This could affect playbook automation for containers that the user cannot view. The vulnerability is possible because the Playbook Automation API accepts a supplied playbook run identifier without verifying that it is bound to the server-provided playbook execution context. The vulnerability requires a running playbook on a container label that the user cannot view.

item.title: CVE-2026-131292 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who can edit and run a playbook on a permitted label could cause Splunk SOAR to return custom-function status and callback state from another playbook run. The issue results from insufficient binding between a custom-function-status request and the playbook run that initiates it.

item.title: CVE-2026-131293 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.3 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to edit and run playbooks could read or overwrite persisted data for playbook runs outside the authorized label, or ownership scope for that user. The affected data can include playbook inputs, prompt and block results, outputs, and secrets that playbooks save in run data. Overwriting the data could corrupt results that paused, scheduled, or parent playbook runs later use. The vulnerability is possible because the playbook automation APIs do not bind data operations to the active playbook run.

item.title: CVE-2026-131294 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who can edit and run playbooks on a container label could associate a custom-function callback with another playbook run. The callback could modify the state of a container outside the authorized scope for that user. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not bind playbook API requests to the trusted playbook run and container context.

item.title: CVE-2026-131295 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to create and run playbooks could start child playbooks on containers outside the authorized label, or repository scope for that user. This could expose container data and affect automation outside that scope. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not bind the identity used to authorize the child playbook run to the parent playbook execution context.

item.title: CVE-2026-131296 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with permission to author and run playbooks could add messages to a different playbook run log and cause that run to fail, including runs outside the labels that the user could access. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify that playbook API requests use the trusted runtime context for the current playbook run.

item.title: CVE-2026-131297 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an operator of a configured identity provider could authenticate as an existing user associated with another configured identity provider. If that account has the "Administrator" Splunk SOAR role, the operator could control the Splunk SOAR deployment. Splunk SOAR does not bind external user accounts to the identity provider that provisions them and authenticates accounts by username without verifying provider ownership. The vulnerability requires more than one configured external identity provider with distinct trust domains and a target username that an operator of a configured identity provider can authenticate through a different provider. For more information see Configure single sign-on authentication (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/configure-single-sign-on-authentication-for-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Manage roles and permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-131298 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with edit permission on a workbook could configure a service-level agreement at only the workbook phase or task level. Splunk SOAR then flags the task as overdue immediately and does not display the configured deadline in the work queue. The incorrect deadline status could obscure genuine deadline breaches. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR treats an absent phase-level or task-level service-level agreement as immediately due when it compares the configured due times. For more information see Define tasks using workbooks (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/7.0.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/define-tasks-using-workbooks) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-131299 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | In Splunk App for Stream versions below 8.1.7, an unauthenticated user who can reach the Splunk App for Stream Representational State Transfer (REST) API on the management port (8089) could upload an Extensible Markup Language (XML) vocabulary file, which lets the vocabulary upload endpoint read local files accessible to the Splunk process or send outbound requests. The vulnerability is possible because the vocabulary upload endpoint parses uploaded XML without an application-level policy that blocks external entity resolution. For more information see About Splunk Stream (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/collect-stream-data/install-and-configure-splunk-stream/8.1/introduction/about-splunk-stream) and restmap.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.3-configuration-file-reference/restmap.conf) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-131300 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | In Splunk App for Stream versions below 8.1.7, a user who can read splunkd_access.log or the _internal Splunk index could recover the Stream forwarder authentication key and use it to impersonate a trusted Stream forwarder. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk App for Stream sends the authentication key in an internal request URL, and Splunk records that URL in splunkd_access.log. For more information see About Splunk Stream (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/collect-stream-data/install-and-configure-splunk-stream/8.1/introduction/about-splunk-stream) and restmap.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.3-configuration-file-reference/restmap.conf) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-131301 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3 | In Splunk App for Stream versions below 8.1.7, an unauthenticated user could cause Splunk App for Stream to reset its in-memory indexer cache. The vulnerability exists because the Splunk Web handler accepts the cache-reset request without requiring a login. For more information see Splunk Stream installation package overview (https://help.splunk.com/en/data-management/collect-stream-data/install-and-configure-splunk-stream/8.0/introduction/splunk-stream-installation-package-overview) and Launch Splunk Web (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.6/administer-splunk-enterprise-with-splunk-web/launch-splunk-web) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-131302 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could turn on the AI chat training-data consent setting through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. The missing authorization is possible because the affected configuration endpoint does not enforce authorization checks.

item.title: CVE-2026-131303 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.1 | In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could obtain limited information about indexes and data sources outside their authorized scope through the assistant. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk AI Assistant does not fully apply authorization controls to all information that it retrieves.

item.title: CVE-2026-131304 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1 | In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0 a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could access data associated with another tenant and cause actions to be attributed to that tenant through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk AI Assistant accepted a client-controlled tenant identifier when selecting the authorization context for a request.

item.title: CVE-2026-131305 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1 | In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could submit client-controlled feature settings through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This could modify limited response metadata outside the expected server-side configuration. The vulnerability is possible because the REST API processes client-supplied feature settings without enforcing the expected server-side configuration boundary.

item.title: CVE-2026-18883 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1 | ServiceNow has addressed an indirect prompt injection security issue that was identified in the Email Response AI Agent of Now Assist for CSM. We are not currently aware of malicious exploitation against ServiceNow instances.
This remediation was deployed centrally to the Email Response AI Agent (Now Assist for CSM) and does not require a platform version upgrade or hot fix; no version-specific backports apply.

item.title: CVE-2026-76532 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could view credentials configured for email notifications in a saved search shared with that user. The vulnerability is possible when email notifications use authentication credentials because the Saved Searches Representational State Transfer (REST) API returns those credentials in clear text. For more information see Search endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/leverage-rest-apis/rest-api-reference/10.6/search-endpoints/search-endpoint-descriptions), Manage knowledge object permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.6/get-started-with-knowledge-objects/manage-knowledge-object-permissions), and Email notification action (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/alert-and-respond/alerting-manual/10.6/configure-alert-actions/email-notification-action) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-76533 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.2
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.2 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17 on Ubuntu and AlmaLinux, an unauthenticated user who obtains a valid Splunk Web session cookie before the affected user logs out could continue using the cookie after logout to access data and perform actions available to that user. The vulnerability is possible because the logout flow does not invalidate the associated session token on affected deployments. The attacker must obtain the valid session cookie before the affected user logs out of Splunk Web. The issue was reproduced in Splunk Enterprise installations on Ubuntu and AlmaLinux.

item.title: CVE-2026-76534 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.7
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.7 | In Splunk Enterprise for Windows versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a user that holds a role with the edit_user capability could create multiple user accounts that share the same user directory. This could expose user-specific configuration between those accounts, let one account modify configuration used by another account, or disrupt features that depend on separate user directories. The vulnerability is caused by improper validation of usernames before Splunk Enterprise performs Windows filesystem operations. Windows removes trailing periods from directory names, so distinct usernames can resolve to the same user directory. For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-76535 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 9.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 9.1 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches through RapidDiag task collection as an authenticated user. With this access, the user could read or modify data and configuration available to that authenticated user. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise accepts an empty shared secret when it authenticates RapidDiag task-collection requests. For more information see Using RapidDiag (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/troubleshoot/9.3/contact-splunk-support/using-rapiddiag) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-76536 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 9.4
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 9.4 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could use an empty clustering shared secret to read and modify clustering configuration through the cluster configuration Representational State Transfer (REST) API endpoint on a standalone instance. This could expose clustering configuration, persist attacker-controlled clustering settings, and disrupt clustering operations. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise accepts the empty clustering shared secret as a shared-authentication candidate on a standalone instance when clustering is turned off.

item.title: CVE-2026-76537 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.3 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.0, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who does not hold a role with either the list_indexer_cluster capability or the edit_indexer_cluster capability could download the cluster manager configuration bundle through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API and access configuration and app files that the cluster manager stages for indexer distribution. The vulnerability is possible because the REST API does not require the list_indexer_cluster or edit_indexer_cluster capability before it sends the configuration bundle. For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation. For more information see Cluster endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/leverage-rest-apis/rest-api-reference/10.6/cluster-endpoints/cluster-endpoint-descriptions) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-76538 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could cause Splunk Enterprise to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with elevated privileges through data model acceleration. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly neutralize caller-supplied data model acceleration values before it places them into generated summarization searches.

item.title: CVE-2026-76539 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could use the search jobs Representational State Transfer (REST) API to access indexed events that the srchFilter setting for the role should hide. The same user could also run internal Search Processing Language (SPL) commands and bypass SPL safeguards for risky commands within indexes that the role can search. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly escape required field values before it includes them in an internally generated search. For more information, see Search endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/rest-api-reference/9.4/search-endpoints/search-endpoint-descriptions), authorize.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/10.4/configuration-file-reference/10.4.5-configuration-file-reference/authorize.conf), and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands).

item.title: CVE-2026-76540 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 9.4.17, 10.0.12, 10.2.9, and 10.4.5, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles can configure a metric alert through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API that runs a search with elevated privileges. The vulnerability lets the user access or modify data and disrupt the Splunk Enterprise instance. The vulnerability occurs because Splunk Enterprise does not enforce the required role-based authorization when it processes metric alert configuration through the REST API. Splunk Enterprise schedules the resulting search with elevated authorization and runs attacker-controlled search processing with that authorization. For more information see About configuring role-based user access (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/about-configuring-role-based-user-access) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-76541 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.8
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.8 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.0, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared data model calculation. When a user who can run a search against the shared data model runs one, the injected SPL can run using the permissions of the user who ran the search. This could expose sensitive credentials to the user who created the shared data model. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not safely neutralize data model calculation fields before it includes them in generated searches. For more information see About data models (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/build-a-data-model/about-data-models) in the Splunk documentation. For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-76542 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.9
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.9 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could trick a user who has an active Splunk Web session into selecting the Top values by time field report on the Search page. The selection could run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches and potentially expose stored credentials and indexed data. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Web does not correctly neutralize user-controlled data when it generates an SPL search for a field report. The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the user by tricking them into opening a link that the attacker creates. The unauthenticated user should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.

item.title: CVE-2026-76543 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared data model. The vulnerability is possible because the Data Model Editor does not properly neutralize data model field names when it builds a preview search. The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will. For more information see Add a regular expression field (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/define-data-model-dataset-fields/add-a-regular-expression-field), Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities), and About the search language (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/search/search-manual/10.4/search-overview/about-the-search-language) in the Splunk documentation.

item.title: CVE-2026-76544 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could cause scheduled metric alert searches to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands and access credentials stored in cleartext. This requires at least one non-internal metric index on the instance. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not fully validate metric alert filter input before using it in a scheduled search.

item.title: CVE-2026-76545 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could determine whether a username exists through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API or Splunk Web and lock out existing user accounts through repeated login attempts. The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise returns different login failure responses for locked existing user accounts and nonexistent usernames.
